$comment: D-MIR-CALLCTX-REFERENCE-HELD-ACROSS-A-NESTED-LOWERING-DUPLICATES-THE-ARGUMENT (P61, lane ml): the RUNNABLE witness for C 6.5.2.2p10 at the by-value aggregate ARGUMENT — an argument expression is evaluated EXACTLY ONCE, and a struct passed by value is not an exception. ★★ THE DEFECT THIS PINS WAS A SILENT MISCOMPILE, not a refusal. `emitByValueStructCallArg` in `src/mir/lowering/hir_to_mir.cpp` lowers the argument's ADDRESS first and pushes the call operands after; when the argument is itself an aggregate-returning call, that lowering re-enters the expression driver and grows the driver's `callCtxs` accumulator. P61 hoisted `callCtxs` from a driver LOCAL to a MEMBER of the one shared driver, so the growth could REALLOCATE it and the per-call context reference held across the lowering dangled — the argument index never advanced in the live context, the pump re-entered on the same argument, and the argument expression was LOWERED TWICE. ✔MEASURED at that state through `dsscp`: `op(mk())` with a counting `mk` exited 5 where gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=c2x -O0`) exited 4. ★★ WHY THE EXISTING CORPUS CANNOT SEE IT, which is why this file exists: the by-value-struct-argument shapes already here (`examples/c/c_int128_float_conv`'s `op(mk(3u,0u))` among them) pass PURE launderers, so evaluating the argument twice yields the identical value and the identical exit code — those examples are green in BOTH directions. Every argument here is instead a call that INCREMENTS A GLOBAL COUNTER, and every term asserts the counter reads exactly 1. THREE AGGREGATE SHAPES because the ABI takes three different routes and fixing one is not fixing the others: a 16-byte struct (InRegisters two-GPR under SysV, ByReference under Win64 — one source reaching both `appendByValueArg` branches across the shipped targets), a 32-byte struct (MEMORY class everywhere, so the by-reference / stack-carrier arm), and `unsigned __int128` (the WIDE INTEGER route into the same `isByValueClass` classification, D-CSUBSET-BITINT-C2-WIDE). PLUS A SCALAR CONTROL: identical nesting, scalar argument, which reaches the call frame through `ScalarPending` and never enters the by-value synthesis — correct before the fix and after it, so a red control means the fixture broke rather than the rule. exit 42 = 10 (16-byte struct once) + 10 (32-byte struct once) + 10 (`__int128` once) + 6 (the scalar control once) + 6 (and the VALUES are right, not merely the counts — a 'fix' that dropped the second materialization's OPERANDS rather than the second EVALUATION would satisfy every counter and corrupt every argument). ANTI-FOLD: every counter is a mutable global and every value derives from the mutable global `gseed`, so nothing here can be pre-computed and reported green without being lowered. ★ WHICH TERM ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATES, ✔MEASURED rather than assumed — ONE of the three, not all three. With the fix reverted this file exits 32, i.e. exactly one ten-point term flips, because a `std::vector`'s capacity only GROWS: the FIRST nested by-value argument in a translation unit is the one whose push reallocates, and after it the vector has room. (✔MEASURED separately on a two-function file: `op(mk())` alone exited 5 against gcc's 4.) So the three aggregate shapes are NOT three independent detectors of THIS defect — they are three ABI routes held against future regressions, and only whichever runs first detects this one. That is also precisely why it was invisible: any by-value struct call earlier in the file hides it. ⓘ AND WHAT THE `release` ARM DOES NOT ADD, ✔MEASURED: the runner compares an optimized arm against the BASELINE's actual exit code, not against 42 — with the fix reverted the release arm reported PASS at exit 32 while the baseline arm reported FAIL. The release arm pins that the shipped pipeline AGREES with the baseline; the BASELINE arm and the MIR-tier pin are the discriminating ones. ✔REFERENCE ORACLE, each probed SEPARATELY on this exact file: gcc 13.3.0 (WSL) compiles and RUNS it to 42 at -O0 and -O2; clang 18.1.3 compiles and RUNS it to 42 at -O0 and -O2; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 compiles and RUNS it to 42 at -O0 and -O2. MSVC casts no vote here: it has no `__int128` at all, which is a MISSING FEATURE rather than a refusal, and the disjunction still binds on the two references that work. ⓘ The MIR-tier twin, which asserts the emitted CALL COUNT rather than a runtime counter and so discriminates on every host with no target to run, is `MirLoweringC.ByValueStructArgumentCallIsLoweredExactlyOnce`.
